gbm_population_evidence.quote: Histopathologically proven diagnosis of IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (GBM, WHO grade 4) according to the 2021 WHO classification (including subtypes such as gliosarcoma).

candidate_evidence.quote: [EXPERIMENTAL] Daily oral azeliragon: Azeliragon to be administered once daily for several days before, during, and after radiation therapy.

Based upon pre-clinical evidence suggesting that azeliragon may enhance the effectiveness of radiation, as well as have a delaying effect on disease progression, this study will combine daily oral azeliragon with radiation treatment

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: The study to be conducted is a phase 2 study in newly diagnosed "unmethylated" glioblastoma.

role_evidence.quote: [EXPERIMENTAL] Daily oral azeliragon: Azeliragon to be administered once daily for several days before, during, and after radiation therapy. (interventions: Drug: Azeliragon)

source_quote.quote: MGMT promoter methylation is negative based on local CLIA-certified commercial laboratory tests.
Histopathologically proven diagnosis of IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (GBM, WHO grade 4) according to the 2021 WHO classification (including subtypes such as gliosarcoma).

coder_notes: Single-arm azeliragon plus radiotherapy (no temozolomide) in newly diagnosed MGMT-unmethylated IDH-wildtype GBM. Radiotherapy is not a registered intervention but is part of the experimental arm, hence regimen combination. IDH-wildtype is diagnostic only (not candidate-matched). Dexamethasone appears only as an outcome measure, not as an intervention, so not listed.
